output.review_comment:
The range check and the switch to rank ceil(p/100*n) (returning the smallest value when p=0) are correct. They fix the real bug, since the old int(p/100*n) was off by one rank, and 9 of the 10 tests now pass.

Blocking: the new `if n % 2 == 0 and p == 50` branch averages the two middle values. It exists only to make test_median_response_time pass (it expects 135 for [120, 80, 200, 150], and 135 isn't one of the inputs). This breaks the docstring, which is the stated source of truth: "The result is always one of the input values: values are never averaged or interpolated." It also breaks the README's promise that every reported value is a real sample.

It changes production behaviour too. latency_summary's p50 would show a made-up value for any even-sized sample set. And it's inconsistent: p=50 averages the middle values, but p=49.9 and p=50.1 use nearest-rank.

Please remove the special case and keep the rest. Then tell the teammate that test_median_response_time conflicts with the documented behaviour (nearest-rank gives 120) instead of hiding the conflict. The PR also needs a description explaining this.
